housing.summary: Bengaluru's rental market is competitive, especially in tech-hub areas like Koramangala, Indiranagar, Whitefield and HSR Layout. One-bedroom flats in central/prime areas command a premium and security deposits are notoriously high compared with the rest of India, often equal to several months of rent. Rental agreements are typically 11-month leases and most tenancies go through brokers or online platforms.

banking.summary: Opening a resident or NRO/NRE bank account requires standard KYC. Foreign nationals typically need a passport, valid visa, proof of local address and a PAN card. Major private and public banks operate extensive branch and ATM networks across the city.
banking.required_docs: Passport, valid visa/residence permit, PAN card, proof of local address; photographs for KYC
banking.banks_named: HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, State Bank of India (SBI), Axis Bank, Kotak Mahindra Bank

schools.summary: Bengaluru has a large selection of international and private schools serving expatriate and local families, concentrated around Whitefield, Sarjapur Road and North Bengaluru near the airport. Options span multiple curricula and admissions are competitive with waitlists at popular schools.

legal_admin.summary: Foreign nationals staying in India beyond 180 days on certain visa categories must register with the local Foreigners Regional Registration Office (FRRO) within 14 days of arrival. Bengaluru has an FRRO office and registration is handled online with an in-person appointment.
legal_admin.registration_step: Register with the FRRO (Foreigners Regional Registration Office) within 14 days of arrival for stays over 180 days

tax_finance.summary: Anyone earning income or opening financial accounts in India needs a PAN (Permanent Account Number) issued by the Income Tax Department. Tax residency is determined by days of physical presence in India, and residents are taxed on worldwide income while non-residents are taxed on Indian-source income.

transport.summary: Bengaluru is served by BMTC city buses and the expanding Namma Metro rail network, supplemented by app-based cabs and auto-rickshaws. Traffic congestion is significant, so many residents rely on the metro for cross-city commuting. Foreign residents can convert a valid foreign driving licence to an Indian licence through the regional transport office.
transport.driving_licence_exchange: Foreign licence can be converted to an Indian driving licence via the Regional Transport Office (RTO) with passport, visa and address proof
transport.healthcare_registration: No universal public registration; residents typically use private hospitals/clinics and private health insurance
